findings.summary: The registry table lists `aws ecr login` as the ECR login command, which is not a valid AWS CLI subcommand.
findings.evidence: ["ECR","`<id>.dkr.ecr..`","`aws ecr login`"]
findings.fix: Replace with `aws ecr get-login-password` (piped into `docker login --username AWS --password-stdin <id>.dkr.ecr.<region>.amazonaws.com`); the deprecated v1 form was `aws ecr get-login`, never `aws ecr login`.

findings.summary: The security chapter carries two near-identical Common Mistakes lists, so the learner reads the same four warnings twice within two pages.
findings.evidence: Page 4: "Root user + docker.sock mounted: one app bug = **full host compromise**" / "No memory limit: container eats host RAM, kernel may kill something else" / "Default json-file logs unbounded: disk fills, host falls over". findings.summary: The layer-transfer fundamentals that explain the registry push/pull flow are taught eight pages after that flow, and after two unrelated chapters.

findings.fix: Move the "layers move once" definition and the pull/push output reading (pages 9-10) to directly follow page 1's tag/push/pull flow, before the security chapter.

findings.summary: The title "Layer Transfer on Pull and Push" misdescribes a page that is overwhelmingly a command reference, with layer transfer appearing only in the final block.

findings.summary: The resource-limit example puts a `#` comment mid-command on a continuation line, which terminates the command before the image name is reached.

findings.fix: End that line with `--memory-swap 512m \` and move the "no swap" remark to the block's note (which already says "same swap value = swap disabled"), or put the comment on the final line.

findings.summary: The "lean, cache-friendly build" Dockerfile copies the entire build stage into an identical base, so the multi-stage split yields no size or hygiene benefit that the surrounding bullets claim.
findings.evidence: ["FROM node:22-slim AS build",...,"FROM node:22-slim","WORKDIR /app","COPY --from=build /app /app"] with bullet "==Multi-stage== + slim base + `.dockerignore` keep the image small"
findings.fix: Copy only the runtime artifacts, e.g. `RUN npm ci` in build plus `RUN npm ci --omit=dev` or `COPY --from=build /app/dist /app/dist` and `COPY --from=build /app/node_modules /app/node_modules`, so the final stage excludes dev dependencies, sources and build caches.

findings.summary: The claim that buildx can never load a multi-arch build locally is outdated — with the containerd image store enabled, `--load` works for multi-platform builds.
findings.evidence: "`--push` is required: buildx cannot load multi-arch locally"
findings.fix: Reword to "`--push` is required unless the containerd image store is enabled; the classic image store cannot hold a multi-platform image".

findings.summary: The buildx example's line continuation splits the platform list into two shell arguments, so the command as printed fails.
findings.evidence: ["docker buildx build \\","  --platform linux/amd64,\\","  linux/arm64 \\","  -t reg/org/app:1.4 --push ."]
findings.fix: Keep the platform list in one token, e.g. `--platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64 \` on its own line (backslash-newline plus the next line's indent inserts a word break after the comma).
